terminal_state_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-15. This file carried a non-terminal awaiting-approval status with emails_sent=false long after the batch's morning package had actually been sent, because nothing in STEP 7/8/9 ever flipped the per-batch pending copy (F38). That left Law #166's pending-batch scan reading a completed batch as an open backlog blocker (F37), which would have skipped the next unattended daily run. Evidence the send really happened, checked before this edit: (1) cron_tracking/sent_scripts_events.jsonl carries a status="sent" row for package 7182ec38 under batch 32e0fcb9; (2) cron_tracking/daily_combined/state.json (top-level mirror) records batch 32e0fcb9 as status=success, emails_sent=true, log_appended=true; (3) the legacy sent_scripts_log.json carries the matching appended entry. NOT verified from the mailbox itself -- no mail tool is available in this environment -- so 'sent' here means the repo's own recorded definition of sent (the logger fails closed without --emails-sent and --approval-file, and both were asserted). The batch is terminal as SENT for its morning package ONLY; the evening package is separately held above and stays open. DELIBERATE WORDING: this note avoids writing the awaiting-approval token literally, because Law #166's check is prose that says to look for a state.json that 'reads' that status -- an agent doing a substring grep rather than parsing the status field would otherwise re-flag this completed batch on the strength of its own explanatory note. The F37 fix makes field-parsing explicit.
